channel.title: Writing — Hasibur Rahman
channel.description: Essays on AI systems, data modeling, Bangla NLP, ASR, backend engineering, and production.

item.title: RAG is not a new engineering discipline
item.description: A vector database is a tool, not a strategy. What backend engineers already know about data modeling is the actual job.

item.title: The invisible characters breaking your Bangla NLP pipeline
item.description: NFC, ZWJ, ZWNJ, and byte-level BPE: how visually identical Bangla words become different token sequences, and what that does to WER and retrieval.

item.title: 13 days of call audio in 1 day
item.description: What production Bangla ASR actually takes: low-bitrate telephony, curated data, a custom tokenizer, and evals that catch what WER misses.

item.title: The RabbitMQ bug that was hiding in a Go channel
item.description: Messages looked lost. They were sitting in process memory. A production debugging story about acknowledgement, buffering, and observability.

item.title: Build the knowledge graph, not the tech stack
item.description: Frameworks are implementations of ideas. A practical way to connect concurrency, memory, and systems knowledge instead of collecting tools.

item.title: From rows to vectors: the more data changes, the more it stays the same
item.description: Vector search did not replace data modeling. It added another access pattern, and the old questions still decide whether retrieval works.

item.title: What 1,200 LeetCode problems don't teach you
item.description: Interviews test whether your thinking is legible. What 1,200 solved problems teach, and what they quietly leave out.

item.title: What is feature engineering, really?
item.description: A feature is a bet about what matters. The job is not adding columns; it is encoding a hypothesis the model can test.

item.title: Why does the sigmoid function actually work?
item.description: The sigmoid function is not decoration. It turns a score into a probability and gives gradient descent a reason to keep moving.

item.title: What is gradient descent, actually?
item.description: Gradient descent is a loop with a budget. Here is what the update rule is actually doing, and where it breaks.

item.title: Is CNN some out-of-the-box magic?
item.description: A convolution is a small, repeated bet about locality. That is why CNNs work, and why they are not magic.

item.title: Can you actually feel what a Transformer does?
item.description: Attention is a lookup with weights. A mental model for what a transformer actually does, without the mystique.
